name: CrossPoint e-reader (sleep screen)
description: CrossPoint e-readers painting a Tesserae dashboard as their sleep screen, over the LAN with no cloud component. The reader draws the image twice, through its GRAYSCALE_LSB and GRAYSCALE_MSB planes, quantising each pixel to 0-3, so the panel is a four-level greyscale ramp and the composition is rendered to the gray_4 gamut rather than to mono. Registering as a generic CircuitPython client left the panel on a mono default and threw those levels away server-side, before the file was written. Pairing is the v1 REST flow: POST /api/v1/device/discover with the reader's derived MAC (locally administered 02: range, so it cannot collide with a real NIC), or the 6-digit code fallback via /register. Steady state is a heartbeat to /status on book close, and a pull of GET /api/v1/device/<id>/frame.bmp for the image itself, which the reader downloads in one request with no redirects.

sleep_interval_s.label: Refresh interval
sleep_interval_s.help: How often the server expects the reader back. The reader pulls its sleep screen when the book closes rather than on a timer, so this mainly decides how long it can be silent before the Devices card calls it stale.
